note: t.Skip/Skipf/SkipNow call sites per package, outside internal/testenv. A COUNT rather than a per-site registry: a registry needs an entry for every one of these, most of which are honest environmental skips, and a list that long becomes a rubber stamp. This can only fall on regeneration; raising it is a hand edit of this file.

raisedBy.why: The upload probe gate needs a real ffprobe to gate with and a real ffmpeg to build media to feed it, and neither is a property of the code. The six sites are: ffprobeOrSkip (no ffprobe, so there is nothing to gate with); sampleMedia's two (no ffmpeg, and an ffmpeg that cannot mux h264/aac); buildSample's one (same, for internal/ffmpeg); and TWO Windows ones -- TestProbeFileReturnsWhenItsContextIsCancelled, whose fixture is a #!/bin/sh wrapper script chosen precisely because it leaves a grandchild holding the stdout pipe, and internal/api's fakeProbe, which is the same shape and which Windows will not execute. Every one is 'this environment cannot run the test', none is 'the thing under test changed'.
raisedBy.alreadyPaidDown: The first draft of the same tests added ELEVEN sites. sampleMedia and buildSample were extracted so that each environmental reason has exactly one site for the whole file instead of one per test, which also took two pre-existing per-test build skips with it. See issue #187: the real fix is making these fail rather than skip when POLYEMESIS_REQUIRE_FFMPEG is set in CI, at which point the four FFmpeg ones can come back out. The two Windows ones need a different fix -- a small helper binary built by the test instead of a shell script -- and are issue #190.

raisedBy.why: The normalise worker now re-runs internal/ffmpeg.ProbeFile's format allowlist on its source before it transcodes anything, which is the SECOND gate an upload the client kept the server from inspecting has to get past. The test that proves an ffconcat script cannot get past it needs a real ffprobe to gate with and a real ffmpeg to build the media the script names, and neither is a property of the code. ONE site, realMediaOrSkip, naming all three environmental reasons at once (no ffmpeg, no ffprobe, an ffmpeg that cannot mux h264/aac); three separate ones would be three free passes for the same condition.
raisedBy.alreadyPaidDown: The same round added a Finding-B test to internal/ffmpeg with two more environmental reasons -- a build that cannot mux AIFF/y4m/GIF, and a build that puts one of them on the allowlist -- and neither is a skip. They log and return, and the parent asserts that at least one of the three formats reached the branch under test, which is a stronger statement than three skips could make. internal/api's new tests added none: they reuse the existing fakeProbe and ffprobeOrSkip sites. Issues #187 and #190 still cover turning the remaining FFmpeg and Windows ones into failures.

raisedBy.why: ONE site, and it is a platform fact rather than an environment one. TestTheStateDatabaseIsNotReadableByOtherAccounts asserts that polyemesis.db and its -wal/-shm sidecars carry no group or other access -- issue #297, where every destination stream key sat in a 0644 file inside a 0755 directory. A Unix mode bit is the whole subject of that assertion and Windows has none: internal/fsperm implements the same INTENT there with an ACL, and fsperm_windows_test.go is where that is asserted. Skipping is therefore not a gap in coverage, it is the assertion being made in the one place it means something. The alternative -- asserting mode bits on Windows -- would pass vacuously, which is the failure this census exists to stop.

ONE site, the same platform fact as the entry above and for the second half of the same fix. TestReopeningAnOlderInstallSecuresTheSidecarsToo asserts that reopening a database whose -wal and -shm already exist at 0644 narrows them -- the case the first #297 fix missed, because SQLite only gives sidecars the database's mode WHEN IT CREATES THEM. Windows has no mode bits; internal/fsperm carries the same intent there through an ACL. Asserting Unix modes on Windows would pass vacuously.

FOUR sites, all in one helper. #674's reproductions need the SHIPPED FFmpeg: requireShippedFFmpeg(t) in internal/rtmpserver skips on -short, on ffmpeg or ffprobe being absent, and on a major version other than 8. The version gate is the load-bearing one -- a developer machine on 9.x runs these green while exercising nothing, which is a pass asserting something it never tested, and the bug they cover only occurs on the pinned 8.1.2. These four replace TWENTY-FOUR: the same preamble was written out in each of six reproductions before being collapsed into one helper, which is why this raise is +4 and not +28. The container suite runs every one of them on 8.1.2, so nothing here is skipped where it matters.

TestAProbeCutShortInTheHeaderReadIsNotAVerdictEither needs a stand-in ffprobe that sleeps until it is killed, so the cancellation lands inside the header read rather than racing a real ffprobe's exit. The stand-in is a #!/bin/sh script and Windows will not execute it. Environmental, and the SAME skip its sibling TestACountThatWasCutShortIsNotAVerdictAboutTheFile already carries for the same stand-in: 'the branch it pins is not platform-specific; the stand-in is.' Issue #190 is the real fix for this family -- a small helper binary built by the test instead of a shell script -- and would take this one back out along with the two it already names.

raisedBy3.why: ONE site, and it is the Windows arm of the test written to close this PR's own refutation. An adversarial verifier found that the ErrNoDuration return formatted a SHADOWED err -- `err := cmd.Run()` shadowed by `if secs, err := countDuration(...)`, whose scope dies before the return -- so the operator was told `it could not be counted: <nil>`. Seventeen mutations and twelve tests missed it, because every one of them asserted the file was REFUSED and the refusal was correct; only the diagnostic was wrong. TestARefusalNamesWhyTheCountFailedRatherThanNil tables all three reachable causes and asserts each names ITS OWN cause. One of the three is 'there is no ffmpeg to count frames with', produced by a stand-in binary that is a POSIX shell script, which Windows will not execute -- the same shape internal/api's fakeProbe already carries in the entry above, and the subject of #265. Environment, not a property of the code.
raisedBy3.alreadyPaidDown: The api-side half of the same fix -- TestTheRefusedRawStreamsBodySaysWhyTheCountFailed -- added NO site: it reads the refusal out of the HTTP 400 JSON through the existing fixture, so it needs no stand-in of its own. The ffmpeg-side table skips once for the whole Windows case rather than once per cause; three separate calls would be three free passes for one condition, which is the rule the entry above sets.
raisedBy3.handEditedRatherThanRegenerated: Same reason as every entry above: -update-skips round-trips this file through a struct with no field for these reasons and deletes all of them. The two numbers were raised by hand.
